series: Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI), every model Epoch scores, by release date
unit: ECI points: linear, unbounded, rescaled so Claude 3.5 Sonnet = 130 and GPT-5 = 150
description: Main series: Epoch's composite capability score for all 270 dated models, with Epoch's 90% bootstrap interval (ci90_low, ci90_high; none for the two anchor models), organization and open/closed-weights group. `other_series` holds training compute of notable models, the lowest inference price at fixed scores, and one series per kept benchmark (percent, 0 to 100), each with dated points sorted by date and a `frontier` flag (a new record by date). Bounded benchmark series also carry `crossings`: the dates the frontier crossed 10%, 50% and 90% of the ceiling. Built by experiments/epoch/build.py; see experiments/epoch/README.md.
method: Item response theory: performance(model m, benchmark b) = sigmoid(alpha_b * (C_m - D_b)). Capabilities C_m, difficulties D_b and slopes alpha_b are fit jointly to every score by non-linear least squares with a ridge penalty, with no time or compute term. Scores enter normalized by each benchmark's random baseline and max-achievable ceiling, as the best score per model group. Models need at least 4 benchmarks. 90% intervals come from 500 bootstrap refits. Source: https://epoch.ai/data/eci-documentation/methodology and https://github.com/epoch-research/eci-public; paper: https://www.arxiv.org/abs/2512.00193.
interpretation: The scale is arbitrary but linear: Epoch means +10 from 100 to 110 to be as impressive as from 140 to 150. There is no maximum. At launch, Epoch found about +5 ECI matched a doubling of METR's time horizon. Absolute slopes mean nothing; changes in slope do. The joint fit is rerun as data arrives, so old models' values can shift slightly between downloads, and the calibration points may be revisited.

caveats: Dates are model release dates, not evaluation dates: Epoch ran many models long after release, so a frontier by release date is drawn in hindsight.
External series mix harnesses and reporters; developer-reported scores (MMLU, GSM8K and the other 2019-2024 sets) are often best-of settings chosen by the lab.
Each point is the best score among a model group's settings on that date (reasoning effort, scaffold, provider), as Epoch's ECI does; the low-effort variants are not separate points.
Frontier means a strictly higher score than every earlier point; ties do not count, and same-day releases yield at most one frontier point.

Each crossing rung is one of: {date} (interpolated linearly between the straddling frontier points, so it usually falls between releases), {date: F, upper_bound: true} (already above at the first dated point F, so F is only an upper bound) or {date: null, open_as_of: L} (not crossed in data ending at L); date is null only when the rung was not crossed. Several sets stopped being updated in 2024 or 2025, so an open rung marks where the data ends, not a plateau. Multiple-choice sets put the 10% rung (and two-choice sets the 50% rung) at or below chance.

Rows with a score but no release date are dropped (counts.undated_rows), as on Epoch's charts. Where some of them beat the dated record, the series says so in `undated_above_record`; there the record and the rungs are lower or later than the full table suggests.

human_baseline.first_at_or_above is the first model at or above the human figure, with its actual release date; human_baseline.interpolated is the ladder-style interpolated date, which no model actually matched.

Superseded series are kept for history; do not join them to their successors. FrontierMath v2 fixed errors in 42% of problems; ProofBench was re-graded on 2026-08-14 with corrected formalizations and a stricter grader, and Epoch marks the v1.0-era rows not comparable, so the file splits ProofBench by grading.
A point with a `note` flags a likely error in Epoch's data, kept as published (Video-MME: VideoLLaMA 3 dated a year before its paper).

In developer-reported series an early report can stand as the record for years; these series have a single frontier point: boolq, lambada. BoolQ's is T5-11B's 91.2 from the T5 paper (Oct 2019) and LAMBADA's MT-NLG 530B (Oct 2021); neither is beaten in Epoch's table, so those frontiers say more about who reported what than about capability.
Benchmark points are dated by the version that scored them, as its CSV gives it; Gemini 2.5 Pro's GA version keeps 2025-06-17, though Epoch dates its group 2025-06-05.

ECI points use Epoch's group dates. For 15 of the 17 ECI models whose versions shipped on different dates, that is the latest version's date (GPT-4 Turbo (Nov 2023) is dated 2024-01-25, though gpt-4-1106-preview shipped 2023-11-06). That matches the index, which takes each group's best score across versions: the earliest date would credit later versions' scores to it.
Epoch's reviews rate HLE, SWE-bench Verified and DeepSWE flawed (see `epoch_review`).
The ECI is refit jointly, so its values move a little with every download; pin to this file's retrieval date when citing.
points_policy: With every point the file would be 542,199 bytes. Every point is kept for the ECI, training compute, inference price, the math series and Epoch-run series. External non-math series with at most 27 points keep every point; larger ones keep only their frontier points (see points_kept), to stay under 400 KB. Counts and crossings use every point. `python3 -I experiments/epoch/build.py --all-points PATH` writes the untrimmed file.

other_series.description: Every model in Epoch's notable AI models table that has a training-compute estimate. Notable means a state-of-the-art advance, over 1,000 citations, historical significance or significant use (Epoch). All domains, not only language models (see `domain`). `frontier` marks a new record for the largest training run to date. `epoch_top5` is Epoch's own 'Frontier model' flag: in the top 5 by training compute when released. `confidence` is Epoch's: Confident within 3x, Likely within 10x, Speculative within 30x.

other_series.series: Lowest LLM inference price to match a fixed benchmark score
other_series.unit: USD per million tokens (Epoch's blend of input and output prices); plot on a log scale
other_series.description: Epoch's data insight 'LLM inference prices have fallen rapidly but unequally across tasks' (Mar 12, 2025): for six benchmarks and several threshold models, the cheapest model at or above that model's score, over time. Each point's note names the capability level it is pegged to; draw and fit one line per (benchmark, threshold_model) (see group_by); pooling the pairings into one curve is meaningless. Lower is better here, so `frontier` marks a new low within each pairing. Dates are Epoch's: GPT-3 appears twice in one pairing (2021-11-20 at $60, 2022-09-01 at $20), so a date can be a later price cut, not only a release. The Arena thresholds are people-voted ratings. The data ends 2025-02-05; Epoch has not extended it.
